A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with IGE renamed ChatGE. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material support comparison, including v1's prompts and v2's Appendices A-C.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 10 custom poker games, including interaction ratings, code correctness, ablations, and error cases in Tables 3-5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and findings in Tables 4-6. Results retained from v1 still qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The script-code-utterance procedure, data synthesis pipeline, and three-stage training strategy remain unchanged under the ChatGE name. Section 4 clarifies that the existing filter rejects code that fails to execute; it does not establish a new filtering procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover interactive development of custom poker games using the same configurable script framework. The 20 seed games and 10 test games remain. Appendix C expands the existing poker illustration without adding an evaluated domain or task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, plus the same ablation variants. The additional user-simulation citations in v2 do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The test set, five-shot comparisons, GPT-4o-mini interactor, LoRA settings, training epochs, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The fuller state-comparison explanation and appendix data breakdown document existing experiments without establishing changed settings.

E4.justification: The component and training ablations, function-level analysis, and two GPT-4o error cases are retained. Appendix A documents the existing ablations' data composition; Appendix C expands the earlier illustrative dialogue without introducing another evaluative analysis.

E5.justification: v2 Section 6.3 newly states that GPT-4o interaction evaluation runs five times and results are averaged. This disclosure does not establish an increase in runs. Both versions retain 40 differently seeded code tests per entry; neither adds variance estimates or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: The numerical results and error-case findings match between v1 Tables 3-5 and v2 Tables 4-6. For example, the full method retains F-Acc 99.0, ESR 100, and Acc 90.0, with unchanged baseline and ablation results.

T1.justification: The interaction-history definition, likelihood objective, and code-merging formalism are retained. v2 makes the likelihood inline and simplifies notation, including omitting explicit S conditioning while retaining the generic script template in the description. No substantive theoretical development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about interactive game development, synthetic training data, progressive training, and the poker case study. Renaming IGE to ChatGE does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations: adapting to another game requires repeating data generation and training, generalization across engines remains difficult, and the current implementation primarily supports text-based games. These qualify applicability; the interpretations of existing experimental results remain stable.

D1.justification: v2 adds seed-function counts and per-ablation data composition in Tables 2 and 7, clarifies filtering, and makes the baseline script-template placeholder explicit. It also removes v1's code/data availability statement and repository URL. The printed evaluator template in Table 14 loses JSON braces present in v1 Table 12.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Delta-Engine discussion and API-Bank citation, while adding six references supporting user simulation, including MINT, DuetSim, and SimUser. Positioning against IDGE remains; its updated publication title represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 renames the framework throughout, edits prose locally, numbers and shortens headings, and organizes supplementary material into Appendices A-C. It adds limitations and a fuller example, but largely preserves the main narrative and section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns presentation: redrawn framework and dialogue figures, a compact first-page example, restructured results and case-study tables, new statistics tables, and boxed prompt displays. The complete dialogue spans Appendix C. These changes extend well beyond renumbering and pagination.

improvement.justification: The added limitations, ablation-data breakdown, five-run reporting, and complete dialogue improve clarity and transparency. However, v2 removes code/data access information and damages the printed evaluator's JSON template, while retaining the same empirical evidence. These documentation gains and reproducibility losses leave the net direction of overall quality unclear.
